We started seeing a spike in 429 responses and elevated p95 latency from our production integration around 13:40 PT. The attached SLO report shows the correlated window (13:40–14:05) with a 12% 429 rate and p95 jumping from 180ms to 1.6s. No code changes on our side during that window.

Subject: Re: Intermittent 429s & p95 latency spike — production

Quick triage update from Eng (Karthik):

What we see:
- The spike correlates with a change in the burst policy rollout that went live earlier this week (automatic safety valve tightening for tenants exceeding short-window average).
- VitaHealth's request pattern has frequent short bursts; the new safety valve reduces allowed burst budget more aggressively than previous policy, causing premature shedding and token-based 429s.
- No backend pod failures or host saturation — CPU/memory and GPU metrics are healthy.

Immediate mitigation (proposed):
1) Roll back the recent safety-valve parameter for the tenant-class that includes VitaHealth to the previous threshold (hotfix) — this will restore prior burst headroom. Estimated impact: restore normal behavior within ~10–15 minutes of rollout.
2) Temporarily increase per-tenant burst credits for VitaHealth for 24 hours while we run controlled canary with adjusted parameters.
3) Post-mortem: adjust policy gating logic so tenants with high short-burst frequency fall into a different smoothing class.

I've attached the current burst-policy-config.yml and a short snippet showing the offending condition. I'll schedule the hotfix at 18:00 PT unless someone objects — this minimizes impact during the demo prep window.

—Karthik

Date: 2027-12-04T18:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Intermittent 429s & p95 latency spike — production (RESOLVED)

Hi Ava — quick update and resolution summary.

Status: We rolled back the tightened safety-valve burst parameter for the tenant-class that includes VitaHealth on 2027-12-03 18:05 PT. Immediate impact: 429s dropped to <0.1% and p95 latency returned to baseline within ~12 minutes. We also applied a temporary +35% burst credit for VitaHealth for 24 hours to cover demo activity.

Root cause: an overly aggressive safety valve rollout that reduced short-window burst headroom for tenants with frequent micro-bursts. This caused policy-based shedding (token rejection) even though backend capacity was sufficient.

Action items:
- Eng (Karthik): schedule policy regression test and change the smoothing class logic (ETA: 2027-12-10).
- CS (Monica): follow up with VitaHealth to confirm demo unaffected and log any residual issues.
- Sales (Naomi): apply the agreed customer credit and confirm billing note.
- Ops (Jordan): prepare one-page exec brief for finance and leadership (due 2027-12-05 EOD).

Apologies for the disruption — we will follow up with a formal RCA and the policy change plan. Let me know if you need raw logs or more traces; attached is a short export we used for the triage.

Thanks for your patience — Jordan
